metadata.title: ICCS 2009, Internationale hovedresultater
metadata.venue: IEA ICCS 2009 (Danish version of IEA international report)

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: ICCS 2009 uses a two-stage cluster sampling design: within each participating country, a sample of at least 150 schools is drawn, then one class is sampled per school (from grade 8, or grade 9 when the country’s typical age in grade 8 is below 13.5), and all students in the selected class participate. The report describes participation standards (school participation and student participation thresholds) and notes the use of replacement schools when needed, which implies complex survey design features in the underlying ICCS database. The text does not specify the exact student weight variable names or replicate-weight procedures used in the Danish presentation, so the weighting implementation details are not recoverable from this excerpt. For analysts using the ICCS international database, standard IEA practice is to apply the provided student sampling weights and to account for the complex design when estimating standard errors and significance.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: This document is a descriptive international results report (a Danish version of the IEA ICCS 2009 international report) and does not present a student-level predictive modeling pipeline that would require explicit plausible-value (PV) handling or a documented missing-data strategy. While ICCS includes Rasch scaling and plausible values for the cognitive test in the underlying study, this excerpt reports mainly descriptive statistics (means, percentages, and scale scores) and does not document how PVs and missing responses were handled in the computations shown here. Therefore, the PV and missing-data handling information is not available in the provided text, representing a reporting gap for methodological transparency at the level of this excerpt.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: Target population is lower secondary students at age ~14 (typically grade 8). If a country’s average age in grade 8 is under 13.5 years, the target grade is changed to grade 9. Within each country, a minimum of 150 schools teaching the target grade are sampled; one class is sampled per school (if multiple grade-8 classes exist), and all students in the selected class participate. Participation standards require approximately 85% school participation and 85% student participation (or a minimum combined participation of 75% = school% × student%), with replacement schools used when necessary; countries not meeting standards are flagged in tables. The excerpt does not specify additional analytic exclusions beyond these participation rules.

data.outcome_summary: ICCS 2009 is an IEA international comparative study of civic and citizenship education among lower secondary students (target age ~14; typically grade 8). The report describes a complex sampling design with schools and one sampled class per school, and it presents international results across 38 countries using a cognitive test (ICCS Civic Knowledge Test) and extensive questionnaires on values, attitudes, and participation. The cognitive test is scaled using a Rasch model and reported on an international scale with mean 500 and SD 100; the report also notes the use of plausible values in the underlying scoring. For the attitudinal and participation domains, the report uses scale scores (often with an international mean set to 50) and item-based percentages, and it highlights that the tables are primarily descriptive rather than ranking claims of “better” outcomes. The excerpt does not provide a student-level predictive modeling framework, nor does it document PV/missing-data handling for the descriptive computations shown here.
data.null_fields_interpretation: This document is a descriptive results report (not an empirical ML paper) and therefore does not contain a predictive modeling design, algorithmic training, or target-variable ML evaluation. As a result, fields related to ML techniques, PV handling in a modeling pipeline, missing-data handling in an ML context, and structured predictive findings are not applicable from the provided text. The excerpt does include detailed assessment design information (sampling, test structure, scaling, and scale-score conventions), but it does not report the kind of model-based performance metrics required for main_findings.
